title: Fort Témiscamingue Trade Store
notes: Parks Canada identifies the store at the southwest end of the historic group. The mapped fur trade diorama supplies an estimate of its location and main axis. It is interpreted with the historic two-store group identified by Roy and Drouin and the large shore-side gabled mass in the 1876 Qualla photograph.
scope: The western timber trade store at the late Obadjiwan trading post, with a plain gabled roof and broad loading doors.
geometryBasis: Parks Canada identifies the store at the southwest end of the historic group. The mapped fur trade diorama supplies an estimate of its location and main axis. It is interpreted with the historic two-store group identified by Roy and Drouin and the large shore-side gabled mass in the 1876 Qualla photograph.
sectionBasis: The 1876 photograph indicates a simple long gabled store near the western shore. The 1888 camp has two stores documented by Roy. This asset represents the western one.
next: Build the long gabled trade store with its alternate front and loading openings.
